extracted_claim: SceneTree processes nodes via ProcessGroups. Each group has owner Node, nodes list, physics_nodes list. _process_group() flushes call_queue, sorts nodes by priority, iterates copy of nodes list, calls NOTIFICATION_PROCESS or NOTIFICATION_PHYSICS_PROCESS. Threaded processing uses WorkerThreadPool::add_template_group_task. Groups have call_queue for deferred messages. _flush_ugc() handles unique group calls. _flush_delete_queue() handles deferred deletion.
implementation_relevance: HSE has no scene tree. Godot's process group architecture is a mature reference for node-based processing.

extracted_claim: Groups are string-keyed sets of nodes in HashMap<StringName, SceneTreeGroup>. Thread-safe via _THREAD_SAFE_METHOD_. call_group_flagsp() copies node list, supports GROUP_CALL_DEFERRED (via MessageQueue), GROUP_CALL_REVERSE, GROUP_CALL_UNIQUE. Input dispatch uses group '_picking_viewports' with _process_picking. SceneTreeGroup has 'changed' flag for lazy sort. nodes_removed_on_group_call tracks nodes deleted during group iteration.
implementation_relevance: Group-based processing with deferred calls is a standard pattern for decoupled communication in scene graphs.

topic: Godot SceneTree Timer and Tween Processing
extracted_claim: Timers are List<Ref<SceneTreeTimer>>. Each timer has time_left, process_always, process_in_physics, ignore_time_scale. process_timers() iterates from back (handles new additions), decrements time_left by delta or unscaled_delta. Tweens follow same pattern. Both support pause-awareness. Timer emits 'timeout' signal when time_left <= 0.
implementation_relevance: HSE has no timers or tweens. This shows how game engines handle time-dependent callbacks.
